what_its_for: This is a birth control patch that prevents pregnancy. It contains two hormones — a progestin (norelgestromin) and an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol) — that work together to stop ovulation (the release of an egg), thicken cervical mucus to block sperm, and thin the lining of the uterus. It may also be used to regulate periods or reduce period-related symptoms in some people.
how_to_take: Apply one patch directly to your skin once a week for 3 weeks in a row, then go one full week without a patch (your patch-free week). Choose a skin area that is clean, dry, and relatively hair-free — good spots include your belly, upper arm (outer area), buttocks, or upper back. Do NOT place the patch on your breasts or on skin that is red, irritated, cut, or very oily. Press the patch firmly with your palm for about 10 seconds to make sure the edges stick well. Change your patch on the same day each week (called your 'change day'). When removing an old patch, fold it in half sticky-side together and dispose of it in the trash — never flush it down the toilet.
dosing: One patch applied to the skin for 7 days (one week). After 7 days, remove the old patch and apply a new one to a different skin location. Do this for 3 weeks total (3 patches). On week 4, do not apply a patch — this is when you will likely have your period. After the patch-free week, start a brand-new 4-week cycle by applying a fresh patch on your scheduled change day.
missed_dose: If you forget to change your patch on time, here is what to do: If it has been LESS than 2 days (48 hours) late — apply a new patch right away and keep your same change day schedule. If it has been MORE than 2 days (48 hours) late — apply a new patch right away, but use a backup method of birth control (like condoms) for 7 days, and your change day may shift to the new day you applied the patch. If you forgot to remove your patch on time at the end of week 3, remove it as soon as you remember. You are still protected from pregnancy during this time. Do NOT skip your patch-free week. If you are unsure what to do, contact your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Keep patches at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Short trips to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) are okay. Store patches in their original sealed pouches until you are ready to use them. Keep patches out of direct sunlight and away from heat. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking cigarettes, especially if you are 35 years of age or older — combining smoking with this patch significantly raises your risk of serious heart and blood vessel problems, including blood clots, heart attack, and stroke. Avoid placing the patch on your breasts or on broken, irritated, or very oily skin. Avoid using lotions, creams, oils, or makeup on the skin area where the patch is placed, as these can prevent it from sticking properly. Avoid activities that may cause excessive sweating or rubbing on the patch location immediately after application, until it is fully secure. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because some medicines (such as certain seizure medications, rifampin, St. John's Wort, and some HIV medications) can make the patch less effective.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency care RIGHT AWAY if you experience any of the following warning signs: sudden severe headache or migraine, vision changes or loss, difficulty speaking or understanding speech, sudden chest pain or shortness of breath, pain or swelling in your leg (especially the calf), numbness or weakness on one side of your body, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), severe stomach or abdominal pain, depression or mood changes, or if the patch falls off and cannot be reapplied. Also call your doctor if you miss two periods in a row (you may want to take a pregnancy test), if you develop severe skin irritation or rash at the patch site, or if you have any questions or concerns about how the patch is working.
when_it_works: If you apply your first patch within the first 5 days of your menstrual period, you are protected from pregnancy right away. If you start at any other time during your cycle, use a backup method of birth control (such as condoms) for the first 7 days of patch use. The patch is most effective when used correctly and consistently — meaning you change it on time every week and do not miss your patch-free week.
special_populations: Women over 35 who smoke should NOT use this patch due to a significantly increased risk of serious cardiovascular events such as blood clots, heart attack, and stroke. This patch is not recommended for women who are pregnant or breastfeeding a newborn. People who have a history of blood clots, stroke, heart attack, certain types of migraines (with aura), liver disease, certain cancers (such as breast or uterine cancer), uncontrolled high blood pressure, or diabetes with complications should talk to their doctor before using this patch, as it may not be safe for them. People who weigh more than 198 pounds (90 kg) should discuss with their doctor whether this patch will be effective enough for them, as it may be less reliable at higher body weights. Teenagers who have had their first period can generally use this patch safely.
